source: AI Video Bootcamp Phase 3, 'Avatar Product Images & Wise Chat' lesson (transcript22.pdf + Avatar Product Images & Wise Chat.txt) - the course's technique for avatar/product ad photography: send a product image and an avatar/scene reference to an AI chat for a detailed image prompt, always naming the exact label text, and 'give me a detailed image prompt where the avatar is holding the product towards the camera making sure the product label is sharp, readable and consistent'. That lesson does NOT teach a paired 'studio vs lifestyle' ad-type split - it is this app's own naming. `studio` mode instead reuses tools/style_bank.json's existing `studio-lighting` style (sourced from the course's separate Style Reference Library PDF, not this lesson) rather than inventing new studio-ad vocabulary the course never taught.
note: Two independent composite modes, not beats - no time dimension, unlike tools/ugc_bank.json's five-beat video ad (see tools/build_ad.py, which this deliberately does not import beat_timings()/product_starts_at() from). `label_accuracy_phrase` is the lesson's own instruction, transcribed verbatim and folded into every shot regardless of mode - a mislabelled bottle fails a studio shot exactly as badly as a lifestyle one. `lifestyle.example_setting` is the lesson's own worked example (a kitchen scene), offered as a default - `setting` stays free text, same as everywhere else in this app, not a closed list of named scenes the course never taught.
label_accuracy_phrase: the product label sharp, readable and consistent

studio.label: Studio composite
studio.note: Product-only, clean background - reuses tools/style_bank.json's existing `studio-lighting` entry rather than inventing new studio vocabulary.

lifestyle.label: Lifestyle composite
lifestyle.example_setting: a bright, modern kitchen with clean white cabinets, soft natural daylight filling the room from a window off-camera
lifestyle.note: The lesson's own worked example: an avatar holding the product toward camera, in a real, lived-in environment - not staged or artificial.
